CONF1.question: A plastic scintillator calorimeter wall is built from square cells, each read one-to-one by its own hemispherical photomultiplier with a bulb about 20 cm in diameter, mounted inside a magnetic shield directly behind the cell. Can such a wall be segmented finely enough that any two particles entering it at points 15 cm apart are always recorded in different cells? End your answer with one line: VERDICT: YES or VERDICT: NO.
